feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector positioning. It reads professionally and is rich in substance, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Well-aligned positioning for digital platform, governance, analytics, and communications leadership in mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Recent Projects, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; several themes/tools appear multiple times. Consolidating would improve clarity and impact.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities: e.g., traffic growth, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain one spelling standard for “organization-wide/organisation-wide”; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; punctuation and bullet formatting are inconsistent, especially in Work Experience and Footer.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and foregrounding the most distinctive strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with a more active, outcome-oriented verb such as “leading” or “delivering.”
- Trim the list of capabilities to avoid sounding like a skills dump; prioritize the most relevant, recent areas.
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds scalable editorial and digital systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Standardize style: use “12+ years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “enterprise web modernization,” “governance,” “analytics,” and “AI-enabled experiences” are already echoed in the subtitle, Core Competencies, and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production” is also repeated in Core Competencies and multiple roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with tighter, parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing broad functions with specific outputs.
- Emphasize the most senior/recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and cross-channel operations.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search…” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills categories; this section should stay high-level, not tool- or category-heavy.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a crisp one-liner with parallel structure.
- Tighten wording: e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” and “modular Drupal 10 microsite built for campaign growth.”
- Where possible, add scale or audience impact instead of feature lists, especially for the microsite and video series.
- Standardize style: use consistent verbs, avoid repeating “Built/Developed,” and spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner prose.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles; this footer should emphasize “selected projects” framing rather than restating duties.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item here; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten around consultant-level value, platform outcomes, and the most strategic initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: merge CMS/front-end/troubleshooting into one outcome-oriented line, e.g. “Implemented Drupal enhancements, front-end updates, and technical fixes across high-traffic public web properties.”
- Emphasize 2–3 highest-value contributions: AI-enabled search, campaign/microsite architecture, and governance/workflow design.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search/discovery improvements, publishing speed, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics” repeats themes already covered in the Director of Digital Media entry.
- Microsite/campaign examples and AI search are already named in Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level unless you add distinct results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national membership organization.”
- Combine the website bullets into one sharper achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes clearer in analytics/governance bullets: add reporting speed, decision-making, publishing consistency, stakeholder adoption, or operational efficiency if you can quantify them.
- Reframe channel/video bullets around strategic expansion, not routine management: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role’s newsletter/social/video management.
- “Built recurring multimedia content” may echo the footer projects and earlier NACo video bullets.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what was built or expanded at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and growth: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine planning/workflow bullets into one stronger outcome-oriented line: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is very close to the Director role’s channel oversight; use “managed” or “ran” to preserve progression.
- Video/livestream language overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling the recurring advocacy series, not general multimedia production.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct value rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:  
  **• Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization**  
  **• Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations**  
  **• Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)**  
  **• Public-sector stakeholder communications**  
  **• Audience-centered content strategy**
- Drop “messaging” and “planning” in favor of stronger operational/leadership terms like “content operations,” “governance,” and “strategy.”
- Keep this section focused on leadership scope; let work experience carry the proof points and scale.
- If space is tight, cut to 4 bullets by removing “Public-sector stakeholder communications,” since that is already clear elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; avoid repeating the same wording.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, not inventory-led; group tools under broader strengths.
- Suggested rewrite: **Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • Web modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Remove “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from this topline section; those fit better in Technical + IT.
- If space allows, replace one generic phrase with an outcome-oriented one tied to recent work, e.g. **Drupal modernization for high-volume public-sector sites**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the Technical + IT section almost line for line, especially platform and coding tools.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and recent project content; keep it here only if phrased distinctly.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic application, not repeat software.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • User behavior analysis • SEO and performance optimization • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Put the highest-value, leadership-oriented terms first; keep tools at the end as enablers.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Executive reporting” for clearer, stronger wording.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to outcomes from recent NACo work: analytics stack expansion, improved reporting, stronger decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; consider consolidating to “SEO and performance optimization.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to senior capability set: “Broadcast-quality studio production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and control-room workflows • Video editing and post-production”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality studio production” to better reflect the in-house studio leadership in the 2022–2024 role.
- Use parallel phrasing and remove filler: keep all items as noun phrases, 4 bullets max.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale/context in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., number of events, recurring series, in-house studio build).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” may duplicate the Director of Digital Media bullet about expanding event production capacity.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize platform depth and ordering rather than repeat broad web skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light qualifiers to show level of use: **Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal’s importance clearer: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise publishing) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid mixing in implementation terms already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly; consider deleting one or making this version more specific.
- “GitHub Pages” may be too minor unless used meaningfully in recent work; cut it if space is tight.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools that support recent platform, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Front-End Development, Integrations & Deployment”
- Rewrite as: “HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions CI/CD”
- If accurate, add one higher-value modern capability tied to recent work, e.g. “structured search implementation,” “workflow automation,” or “serverless scripting”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for cleaner phrasing unless ATS targeting specifically requires them

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; keep this section as a tighter tools list, not a repeat
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if space is tight

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more category-led.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project and work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest/relevant tools first; if Airtable and Power Automate are most current, lead with them.
- Consider dropping one lower-value PM tool if not used recently; too many overlapping platforms can dilute credibility.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to impact, e.g. “used to build editorial planning, approvals, and cross-team communications workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams may feel low-signal unless collaboration tools are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than a capability statement. Because recent roles already emphasize email leadership, this item should stay concise and signal enterprise-level engagement systems.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten phrasing to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light context instead of more tools: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, segmentation and member communications**
- Put the strongest/current platform first; if Dynamics 365 is most recent or strategic, keep it first as listed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter scale or email leadership here; that is already covered well in the NACo work experience entries.
- “Multi-channel communications” and “email newsletters” already appear elsewhere, so this line should remain platform-focused rather than descriptive.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo work bullets. Tighten it to emphasize technical platforms rather than broad capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a pure tools stack: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console**
- Replace broad terms with sharper, technical labels: change **SEO** to **technical SEO / search performance** and **Dashboarding** to **reporting dashboards / KPI reporting**
- Remove **A/B testing** unless you can support it with a platform or outcome elsewhere; if retained, use **experiment design** or name the tool used
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent relevance: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with Topline Skills [3]; consider trimming one of the two or making this section tools-only while leaving strategy/capability language in Topline Skills.
- “SEO” is also implied by analytics/performance work in recent roles, so keep it specific to avoid repetition.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” or scale from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia communications.”
- Add clearer contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If available, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this role as launching or early producing of the series.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” repeats later operations/governance themes; keep this version lighter and more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around the standout achievement first: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Tighten the rest into one impact-oriented clause: “Coordinated innovation and research projects that supported county-focused programs and policy initiatives.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer scope: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one metric or concrete output: number of episodes, audiences reached, projects supported, or types of materials produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
- Avoid overemphasizing video or broad digital operations here, since those are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere, so tighten it to tool-specific skills and keep higher-level production language in recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Split tools from workflows; lead with recognizable software: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, resume-style terms: “Livestream studio workflows” → “Studio livestream production”; “Podcast production” → “Podcast editing & production”
- If accurate, add adjacent tools only if used regularly and not listed elsewhere (e.g., OBS, vMix, StreamYard) to increase specificity
- Consider revised line: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Studio livestream production • Podcast editing & production”
